title: The Bible
sample_locations: Leviticus 23 (festival law, gch113 — Phase 1 truncation flag)
Numbers 26 (census lists, gch143 — Phase 1 truncation flag)
1 Chronicles 6 (81-verse genealogy, gch344 — Phase 1 truncation flag)
why_modernization_needed_or_not: KJV's 1611 English is a genuine barrier for a modern reader, so a modern column is needed — but the current modern-en is verbatim copyrighted NIV with ~166 verses deleted across 92 chapters and 32 chapters of displaced content, so it must be replaced rather than repaired.
best_human_candidate: Berean Standard Bible (BSB), Berean Bible Translation Committee / Bible Hub, complete Bible, 2022 (3rd printing 2022, 4th 2025)
next_action: Get a second opinion on the verbatim-NIV finding and decide whether to pull or replace bible-modern-en.json in production, then import BSB from USJ/USFM into the existing 6,704-paragraph skeleton as the modern column.
critical_flag: LIVE PRODUCTION COPYRIGHT EXPOSURE: bible-modern-en.json verified verbatim NIV (2011, Biblica, all rights reserved). Biblica permits at most 500 verses / <25% of a book without written permission; this file is the complete 66-book text (~31,000 verses) inside a paid commercial product. Needs urgent legal/product attention independent of this audit's editorial timeline.

title: The Divine Comedy
sample_locations: Paradiso 20 (ch87) paras 44-49 outlier + Paradiso 33 (ch100) paras 38-48 finale
why_modernization_needed_or_not: Longfellow's 1867 blank verse with heavy inversion is a real barrier, and the modern-en removes it evenly across all 100 cantos while keeping Dante's images, similes, proper names and doctrinal precision.
next_action: Fix the Inferno 1.13 logic reversal and the dropped Purgatorio 15 simile, then sweep the 5 remaining truncation flags for the same class of dropped image.

title: Paradise Lost
sample_locations: Book 9 paras 100-103 Eve's soliloquy + Book 12 paras 74-76 expulsion/ending
why_modernization_needed_or_not: Milton's Latinate suspended syntax is a genuine barrier and Books 8-12 prove it can be removed without losing the epic register, but Books 1-7 are only de-lineated Milton and deliver none of that benefit.
next_action: Re-run Books 1-7 to the Books 8-12 standard (~46,000 source words); leave Books 8-12 untouched.
critical_flag: Structural: books 1-7 are near-verbatim de-lineated Milton (avg similarity 0.77-0.87, 291 near-identical paragraphs), books 8-12 are genuinely modernized (avg 0.53-0.61, zero near-identical paragraphs). Phase 1's book-wide summary stat masks this split; a per-section check is needed for any long multi-part work.

title: Beowulf
sample_locations: Fitt I paras 0-5 opening + Scyld's funeral
Fitt XLI paras 0-2 Swedish wars digression
Fitt XLIII paras 2-4 barrow and closing lines
why_modernization_needed_or_not: Hall's 1892 imitative-alliterative diction is impenetrable in places, and modern-en removes it well in Fitts I-XXXII while keeping verse lineation and kennings; Fitts XXXIII-XLIII were left essentially unmodernized.
best_human_candidate: Ernest J. B. Kirtlan, prose (1913) - fallback only, not recommended as a replacement
next_action: Re-run the modernization pass over Fitts XXXIII-XLIII only; fix the 'True men are not able' mis-parse in Fitt I and the added 'iron bands' in Fitt XII.
critical_flag: Same split-quality pattern as Paradise Lost: Fitts I-XXXII genuinely modernized, Fitts XXXIII-XLIII barely touched (archaic diction like 'bale-woe', 'puissant prowess', 'atheling' still standing). Completeness itself is good (no digressions cut).

title: Faust, Part One
sample_locations: ch2 Prelude on the Stage paras 3-4 (omission)
ch4 Night para 0 opening monologue (truncated source)
ch8 Auerbach's Cellar paras 40-51 Song of the Flea
ch18 Margaret's Room para 0 spinning song
ch26 A Gloomy Day paras 6-11 + ch27 Night Open Field paras 4-9 (misalignment)
why_modernization_needed_or_not: Unanswerable as it stands: original-en is not the Bayard Taylor verse translation the registry credits, it opens Chapter 4 mid-sentence, and 49 of 895 paragraphs carry untranslated German and OCR debris, so modern-en's defects are all downstream of a broken source.
best_human_candidate: Bayard Taylor, Faust: A Tragedy, Translated in the Original Metres (1870-71)
next_action: Escalate to Anders, then replace original-en with the real Taylor text from Gutenberg #14591 and regenerate modern-en and modern-da from it - do not patch the current modern-en.
critical_flag: original-en is mislabeled/corrupt: registry credits Bayard Taylor's verse translation, but the file is an OCR'd prose crib, missing Faust's opening monologue (ch4 starts mid-sentence), 49/895 paragraphs contain untranslated raw German and OCR debris, and modern-en duplicates one speech and misattributes another.

title: Richard III
why_modernization_needed_or_not: Shakespeare's compressed verse and obsolete idiom are a genuine reader barrier, and modern-en removes it while keeping Richard's ironic, self-delighting direct address intact.
best_human_candidate: Play On Shakespeare / ACMRS Press — Richard III, modern verse translation by Migdalia Cruz
next_action: Scoped fix pass on 4.2 p37, 5.3 p114, Zounds/Exeunt consistency, and repair orphaned speaker-tag paragraphs in 4.4 in both English editions together.
critical_flag: Structural bug: 4.4 has orphaned speaker-tag paragraphs (a bare 'QUEEN MARGARET.' line with content split across neighboring paragraphs) — a source-parsing artifact in original-en mirrored into modern-en; must be fixed in both files in lockstep or alignment breaks.

title: Coriolanus
why_modernization_needed_or_not: Knottiest syntax and heaviest Roman political vocabulary of the late tragedies; modern-en preserves patrician/plebeian register contrast well but flattens the play's central keyword.
best_human_candidate: Play On Shakespeare / ACMRS Press — Coriolanus, modern verse translation by Sean San José
next_action: Targeted 'voices' pass across 2.1-3.3 (keep the voices/votes pun, gloss on first use rather than global substitution), fix 3 garbled clauses.

title: Cymbeline
why_modernization_needed_or_not: Late-Shakespeare syntax plus a four-strand romance plot makes a modern companion essential, but modern-en stops doing the work in Act 5, exactly where the plot is untangled and readers need it most.
best_human_candidate: Play On Shakespeare / ACMRS Press — Cymbeline, modern verse translation by Andrea Thome
next_action: Re-modernize 5.3-5.5 (~6,700 words, 23.5% of the play) to the depth of Acts 1-4; restore an omitted clause at 1.1 p5.
critical_flag: Act-level modernization drift invisible to Phase 1 book-level stats: Acts 1-4 average ~0.30 similarity (real rewrite), Acts 5.3-5.5 sit at 0.65-0.68 (barely more than thou->you substitution) — 23.5% of the play. pct_identical_long_paragraphs is only 0.2% so the existing flag set reports this book as clean.

title: The Odyssey
why_modernization_needed_or_not: Butler's 1900 prose is the best PD Odyssey but still Victorian, so a modern layer earns its place, and 20 of 24 books deliver one well.
best_human_candidate: Samuel Butler, The Odyssey (prose, 1900) — already the core text; no better PD option found
next_action: Redo Books 2, 9, 14, 19 (currently Butler with only name/spelling swaps) to the standard already set by Books 1, 12, 20.

title: Ulysses
sample_locations: Ep14 Oxen of the Sun paras 0,2,10,30
why_modernization_needed_or_not: Ulysses is a rights-clear English original whose difficulty is allusion, register and parody rather than archaism — untranslatable, and every clarification found deletes something the book is made of.
next_action: Retire or relabel ulysses-modern-en and spend the budget on an annotation/gloss layer plus per-episode orientation notes over the 1922 text.
critical_flag: Two-thirds of the book (episodes 11-18, 67% of total words) received only a thin glossary pass (0.18% token change in Penelope); where it does intervene it does damage — 'fearful jesuit'->'cowardly Jesuit' (mistranslation), 'Christine'->'Christ' (kills a joke), 'throwaway'->'religious leaflet' (breaks the Gold Cup pun), 'But he adds'->'But Aristotle adds' (invented attribution).

title: The Epic of Gilgamesh
why_modernization_needed_or_not: Every readable modern Gilgamesh is in copyright and every public-domain one is partial/lacunose, so an in-house modern edition earns its place — once the base text's provenance is settled.
best_human_candidate: Getty & Kwon, Compact Anthology of World Literature (Thompson + Muss-Arnolt trans., ed. Laura J. Getty) — selections only
next_action: Establish what gilgamesh-original-en actually is before touching modern-en.
critical_flag: PROVENANCE/RIGHTS RISK: original-en shares verbatim wording with a web compilation asserting '© 2014 Jason Colavito, all rights reserved'; other passages are absent from that compilation; lacuna markers appear silently removed/filled; registry lists translator:null, year:null. modern-en also shows recurring collapse of formulaic repetition (5-fold funeral refrain, 12 double-hours reduced) plus one invention ('Now sleep!' -> 'Let me test you. Try not to sleep.').

title: The Iliad
why_modernization_needed_or_not: Butler 1898 is the best PD Iliad but thoroughly Victorian, so a modern edition is worth having — and the one currently shipped is not one.
best_human_candidate: Samuel Butler, The Iliad (prose, 1898) — already the core text; Lang/Leaf/Myers read and rejected as more archaic
next_action: Produce a genuine modern-English Iliad over Butler, or retire modern-en and ship Butler plus glosses — stop labelling a near-duplicate 'Modern English'.
critical_flag: modern-en is essentially Butler 1898 with Roman->Greek god-names and Americanized spelling: word ratio 1.00 in 14/24 books, 34 byte-identical long paragraphs (15 in the Catalogue of Ships), zero paragraphs below 72% of source length across all 1,137 pairs. Archaic vocabulary (gainsay, behests, wherewith, vouchsafed, hard by) survives unchanged.

title: The Aeneid
why_modernization_needed_or_not: Dryden's 1697 couplets are genuinely inaccessible, so modernization is needed — but the current edition only de-versifies him, putting Virgil two removes away before the work even starts.
best_human_candidate: J. W. Mackail, The Aeneid of Virgil (prose, Macmillan 1885) — complete; alternative: Theodore C. Williams blank verse, 1908
next_action: Rebase the English core on Mackail 1885 prose (or Williams 1908 verse), modernize from that, keep Dryden as a third edition labelled as the English poem it is.
critical_flag: modern-en is de-versified Dryden (elisions expanded, thou-forms normalized, line breaks removed) with 17th-c diction left standing (irremeable, suborned, prevented his formed excuse, void of breath), uniform across all 12 books. (Out-of-scope aside noted by the batch, not part of this English audit: the-aeneid-modern-da is 38,520 words against a 107,470-word source, a 64% shortfall not caught by books/scan-report.md's book-ratio metric.)
